1.2 OVERALL CONDITION: Unit generally cluttered; tenant stated they are in process of packing due to relocation. Clutter did not prevent inspection of affected areas.

1.3 PETS: None observed.

1.4 SMOKE/CO DETECTORS: Smoke detector present in hallway, no battery (unit removed, sitting on counter). CO detector not present. Note: landlord states CO detector was installed in 2023 but tenant reports it was removed during ceiling repair in March and never replaced.

---

SECTION 2 – WATER INTRUSION / MOISTURE

2.1 LIVING ROOM – CEILING (northwest corner):
- Active water stain, approx. 18" x 24", yellowish-brown discoloration.
- Paint bubbling in a 6" diameter area near the center of the stain.
- No active dripping at time of inspection.
- Moisture meter reading: 28% on ceiling surface (measured through paint; readings above 15% considered elevated).
- Photo refs: P-101, P-102, P-103 (see photo log attached).

2.2 LIVING ROOM – WALL (west wall, below ceiling stain):
- Vertical crack in drywall, approx. 14" long, hairline to 1/8" wide at widest point.
- Staining on wall surface extending from ceiling down approx. 10".
- No visible mold growth on wall surface at time of inspection.
- Photo refs: P-104.

2.3 KITCHEN – CEILING (above sink):
- Old water stain, approx. 12" x 10", dried, no active discoloration observed.
- Surface appears patched and painted over; paint mismatch suggests previous repair.
- Moisture meter reading: 9% (within normal range).
- No photo taken per inspector discretion (stain not active).

2.4 BATHROOM – VENTILATION:
- Exhaust fan not operational (switch does not activate fan; humming sound but no blade rotation).
- Visible dust accumulation on fan grille.
- Moisture on ceiling above shower stall (condensation droplets present at time of inspection).
- Tenant reports fan has been non-functional for approx. 2 months.
- Photo refs: P-105, P-106.

The Inspection Form has inspection form ID IF-2025-0148. Record status: current.

2.5 CLOSET – BEDROOM 2 (interior, north wall):
- Musty odor detected upon opening closet door.
- Dark staining on baseboard, approx. 4" high, running length of 3 feet.
- Carpet in closet damp to touch (moisture meter reading: 22% on carpet surface).
- No visible mold growth on baseboard; tenant reports recurring musty smell since winter.
- Photo refs: P-107, P-108.

---

SECTION 3 – MOLD / BIOLOGICAL GROWTH

3.1 VISIBLE MOLD – BEDROOM 1 (southeast corner, floor level):
- Black/green speckled growth on baseboard and adjacent drywall, approx. 8" x 6" area.
- Growth appears active (not dried/cracked).
- Tenant reports area was previously cleaned with bleach by property management in April 2025, but growth returned within 3 weeks.
- Photo refs: P-109, P-110, P-111 (close-up with scale).

3.2 VISIBLE MOLD – LIVING ROOM WINDOW SILL (east window):
- Small patch of black mold on wood sill, approx. 2" x 1.5", near corner.
- Condensation on window glass at time of inspection (outside temp ~58°F, inside ~72°F).
- Photo ref: P-112.

3.3 AIR QUALITY TESTING: Not performed during this inspection. Recommend follow-up air sampling if clinically indicated (tenant reports respiratory symptoms; see Section 6).

---

SECTION 4 – ELECTRICAL

4.1 BEDROOM 2 – OUTLET (south wall, near door):
- Outlet cover plate missing; outlet visibly loose in box.
- When tenant plugged in a lamp, outlet sparked (tenant reports this occurred on 06/08/2025; not reproduced during inspection).
- No GFCI present (bedroom not required, noted for completeness).
- Photo refs: P-113, P-114.

4.3 LIVING ROOM – CEILING FIXTURE:
- Light fixture present, no cover plate. Bulb exposed.
- Fixture pulls away from ceiling approx. 1/2" at the mounting bracket; screws appear stripped.
- Wiring visible through gap (no junction box cover present).
- Tenant states fixture wobbles when light is turned on/off.

4.4 HALLWAY – SMOKE DETECTOR:
- Smoke detector mounted on ceiling near bedroom 1 door.
- Detector beeped once during inspection (low battery warning pattern – single chirp, approx. every 60 seconds).
- No visible date of manufacture on unit; tenant unsure when battery was last replaced.
- Recommend tenant contact property management for battery replacement or unit replacement.
- Photo ref: P-119.

---

SECTION 5 – PLUMBING

5.1 KITCHEN – SINK (under-sink area):
- Active leak at cold water supply line connection to faucet. Dripping approx. 1 drop per 5 seconds at time of inspection.
- Water stains on cabinet floor (approx. 6" x 8" area, dark brown, appears old – dried).
- Cabinet floor soft to touch in stained area (possible water damage to MDF).
- Tenant placed a plastic container under the leak to catch drips; container was approx. 1/4 full.
- Photo refs: P-120, P-121.

5.2 BATHROOM – TOILET (master bath):
- Toilet runs continuously after flushing (approx. 2 minutes before stopping; then re-starts intermittently).
- Flapper appears worn/cracked (visible when tank lid removed – photo taken).
- Water level in tank slightly above overflow tube.
- Tenant reports toilet has been running for approx. 1 month; they have been jiggling the handle to stop it.
- Photo refs: P-122, P-123 (tank interior).

5.3 BATHROOM – SHOWER HEAD (master bath):
- Low water pressure noted at shower head (approx. 1.5 gallons per minute measured with bucket test – below typical 2.5 gpm).
- Shower head appears clogged with mineral deposits (white buildup visible on nozzles).
- No other plumbing issues noted in this bathroom.
- Photo ref: P-124.

Inspection Form inspection_date 2025-06-10 date. Record status: current.

5.4 WATER HEATER (closet in hallway):
- Water heater located in hallway closet. Unit appears older (no visible manufacture date; serial number begins with "99" suggesting 1999).
- Slight rust at base of unit, no active leak.
- Temperature set to "B" (approx. 120°F per tenant's understanding).
- Pressure relief valve has no discharge pipe (open end, not directed to drain). Noted as potential safety hazard.
- Photo refs: P-125, P-126.

SECTION 6 – HEALTH / SAFETY / TENANT CONCERNS

6.1 TENANT-REPORTED SYMPTOMS:
- Tenant (female, age 34) reports recurring headaches, nasal congestion, and coughing since moving in (Jan 2025).
- Symptoms worsen when at home; improve on weekends when away.
- Tenant has not seen a doctor for these symptoms but states she "has been thinking about it."
- No visible respiratory distress during inspection; tenant appeared in good health at time of visit.

6.2 TENANT-REPORTED PESTS:
- Tenant reports seeing "small ants" in kitchen near sink (approx. 2-3 per day, starting June 1, 2025).
- No ants observed during inspection (inspection time: 10:15 AM – 11:45 AM).
- No droppings or nests observed in kitchen cabinets or along baseboards.
- Tenant has not reported pests to property management.

6.3 OTHER TENANT CONCERNS (verbatim, as reported):
- "The front door doesn't seal right – I can feel air coming in."
- "The bedroom window upstairs won't stay open on its own."
- "The dishwasher has a weird smell when it runs."

9.4 HALLWAY BATHROOM (shared between bedrooms):
- Sink: hot water handle is hard to turn (stiff). Cold handle turns freely. No leaks observed under sink. Drain stopper is missing – tenant uses a rubber stopper.
- Toilet: runs intermittently (approx. every 2–3 minutes). Flapper appears worn. Tenant states she has to jiggle the handle to stop it sometimes. Water level in tank is above the overflow tube.
- Tub/shower: caulk along tub edge is cracked and peeling on the front side. Grout between tiles on the shower wall has several gaps (mold present in gaps, dark spots). Showerhead has moderate mineral buildup. Water pressure is adequate.
- Vent fan: operates but is noisy (rattles). Tenant states it has been noisy since she moved in. Fan cover is loose on one side.

- Tenant reported that the outlet above the counter on the east wall (near the toaster) "sometimes just stops working." During inspection, the GFCI outlet in the kitchen tripped when the toaster was plugged in and turned on. Reset button works. Plugged toaster back in – outlet held for approx. 2 minutes, then tripped again.
- Same outlet is warm to the touch after tripping. No discoloration or burn marks visible on the faceplate.
- The GFCI outlet appears to be newer than the other outlets in the kitchen (white, no paint overspray). No date code visible.
- This is the same circuit as the warm breaker noted in 10.1.
- Photo refs: P-148 (GFCI outlet), P-149 (toaster plugged in).

10.3 SMOKE / CO DETECTORS (continued from 8.3):
- Basement smoke detector (near furnace): present, test button works. No chirp. Tenant states she has not changed the battery since moving in (Dec 2024). Battery date code on the installed battery is 2021 – recommend replacement.
- No CO detector in basement. Per code, not required but recommended if tenant spends time in basement.
